mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Clio 0.9 TCe engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Renault Clio 0.9 TCe engine replacement typically costs £1,500-£2,800 supply-only for a rebuilt unit (H4B 400 / H4B 408 / H4B 412), with used engines from £400-£900. Fitting adds approximately £520-£715 in labour (8-11 hours at independent specialist rates). Main dealer fitted prices are typically 30-50% higher.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Clio 1.0 TCe engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Renault Clio 1.0 TCe engine replacement costs £2,500-£4,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit (H4D 400 / H4D 450 / H4D 480), with used engines from £500-£1,400. Fitting adds approximately £520-£780 in labour (8-12 hours). Newer Clio V models have higher value, making replacement more financially viable.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Renault Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include a rattling noise from the timing cover on cold start, metallic chatter, rough idle, hesitation, loss of power, and poor fuel economy. Some owners report chain slap or whip noise when lifting off the throttle, particularly going uphill. If the chain skips teeth, the engine may go into limp mode or fail to start altogether.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Clio 0.9 TCe sensitive to oil changes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The TCe 90 engine's timing chain tensioner is hydraulically operated, relying on oil pressure to maintain correct tension. If the oil becomes contaminated or the oil galleries become blocked (due to missed or poor-quality oil changes), the tensioner may not receive sufficient oil pressure, leading to chain stretch and eventual failure. Use the correct 5W-40 oil meeting Renault RN 0700 specification.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Clio IV 0.9 TCe (2012-2016) worth £3,000-£6,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,500-£2,800 plus fitting may represent 50-80% of the vehicle's value. If the car is otherwise in good condition with low rust and a strong gearbox, replacement can still be worthwhile - especially with a 12-month warranty. For vehicles under £4,000, a used engine or timing chain repair may be more cost-effective. For Clio V 1.0 TCe (2019+) worth £8,000-£18,000, replacement is almost always viable.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 0.9 TCe and 1.0 TCe engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 0.9 TCe (H4B) is an 898cc three-cylinder producing 76-90hp, fitted to the Clio IV (2012-2019). The 1.0 TCe (H4D) is a 999cc three-cylinder producing 90-100hp, introduced with the Clio V in 2019. Both share the same basic architecture - three cylinders, 12 valves, DOHC, turbocharged - but the 1.0 TCe offers improved torque delivery (160Nm vs 135Nm) and better efficiency.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Renault Clio 0.9 TCe arrived in 2012 with the fourth-generation Clio IV, replacing older naturally aspirated 1.2-litre petrol units with a modern three-cylinder turbocharged engine. In 2019, the Clio V replaced the 0.9 TCe with an updated 1.0 TCe, offering improved power and efficiency while retaining the same three-cylinder turbo character. The TCe engine family has become the core petrol offering across the Clio range.

milestones.description: Clio IV launched with 0.9 TCe 90 (H4B 400, 898cc, 90hp) and 1.2 TCe 120 (H5F 400)
0.9 TCe 76hp (H4B 408) and 0.9 TCe 90hp (H4B 412) variants added to the range
Clio V launched, replacing 0.9 TCe with 1.0 TCe (H4D 400, 999cc, 90-100hp)
1.0 TCe 100hp (H4D 450) introduced with improved torque delivery
1.0 TCe updated for Euro 6d emissions compliance (H4D 480)

commonProblems.h2: Renault Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Renault Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe engine family is a three-cylinder turbo unit that offers excellent efficiency, but it has well-documented failure points. Timing chain tensioner failure and stretch are the most significant issues across both the 0.9 and 1.0 litre variants. The TCe 90 is sensitive to oil changes, and regular maintenance is critical to avoiding catastrophic engine failure. Rebuilt Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the Renault Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe Suffers Premature Chain Wear
problems.affectedModels: Renault Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe (H4B 400 / H4B 408 / H4B 412 / H4D 400 / H4D 450 / H4D 480, 2012-present)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can fail, causing the chain to become loose and skip teeth on the sprockets. Owners report chain slap and whip noise, particularly when lifting off the throttle. The oil galleries that feed the tensioner may become blocked if oil changes are missed. The TCe 90 is sensitive to oil changes - as long as these have been done, you should be relatively safe.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, tensioner, guides; replace oil jet
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early before valve/piston damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip, inspect, replace damaged valves/guides, machine head
repairOptions.longevity: If timing jump has caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: For a Clio 0.9-1.0 TCe with timing chain rattle, get a specialist inspection immediately. If caught early, a chain and tensioner replacement (£500-£1,000 at a specialist) can save the engine. If the chain has already jumped, a cylinder head rebuild or full engine replacement may be required. For cars with high mileage (80,000+) and multiple issues - timing chain, oil consumption, carbon buildup - a replacement engine with upgraded components and warranty often represents better long-term value than piecemeal repairs.

problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Carbon Buildup - Direct Injection Issues on the Clio TCe
problems.rootCause: The TCe engines use direct fuel injection, which can lead to carbon buildup on the intake valves. This is because fuel is injected directly into the cylinder, not across the intake valves, so detergents in the fuel never clean them. Excessive oil consumption has also been reported on higher-mileage units.
